items.title: The slot decides the class

states.label: Verb slot
states.sm: E uō le tama ma le teine.
states.en: The boy and the girl are friends.
states.note: *Uō* follows a tense particle, so it is a verb here.

states.label: Noun slot
states.sm: E alofa le tama ʻi lana uō.
states.note: *Uō* follows the possessive form in the article’s place, so it is a noun here.

items.caption: The word brings the ability to fill either slot. The sentence decides which slot it fills and therefore its class.

items.title: Classify from the slot

data.question: What class does the named word have here?

prompts.sm: E uō le tama ma le teine.
prompts.why: It stands after the general particle, in the verb slot.

prompts.sm: E alofa le tama ʻi lana uō.
prompts.why: The possessive form stands in the article’s position, before a noun slot.
It follows the change particle in the verb slot.

items.intro: Read the word named with each sentence, then use what stands in front of it.

items.title: One name, place or people

states.label: The place
states.note: A place name referring to a place takes *ʻi*.

states.label: The people
states.note: The same name referring to people takes *iā*.

items.caption: A name takes *iā* when it refers to a person or a people. A place name used for its place keeps *ʻi*.
